children: By Kit Norton

Fresh off announcing a new private artificial-intelligence company in partnership with Palantir Technologies, autonomous drone maker Ondas posted record quarterly revenue and forecast it can break even sooner than expected.

The provider of artificial-intelligence-powered autonomous drone systems on Thursday said that third-quarter revenue surged 1,558% to a record $167.5 million, easily beating estimates of $148 million from Wall Street.
Ondas added that its backlog increased 36% from the second quarter to $835 million.

Along with the robust revenue and backlog growth, Ondas said it now expects full-year revenue of "at least" $550 million, with revenue of more than $250 million in the fourth quarter. The company previously forecast full-year revenue of $525 million to $550 million.

While turning a profit remains an issue for Ondas, the company said it now expects full company adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or Ebitda, of break-even in next year's third quarter. Prior to releasing its third-quarter results, Ondas expected profitability by the end of 2027.
"This quarter demonstrates the growing benefits of Ondas' integrated operating platform," CEO Eric Brock said in the earnings release.

Brock added that Ondas has gained access to larger customers and that the company's "next phase" will be defined by how well it can deliver on customer commitments, integrate its capabilities, and convert demand to sustainable growth and improving profitability.
The solid earnings come as Ondas last month announced the creation, in partnership with Palantir, of a new private AI company called Regna AI.

The new company is initially wholly owned by Ondas with Palantir providing the AI model-training infrastructure. Regna AI is geared toward institutional partners to help customers develop and deploy sovereign "mission-specialized fine-tuned AI models."
Palantir CEO Alex Karp said in the media release last month that Regna AI will give institutions access to sovereign AI "that could never justify building a frontier model of their own."
The new venture between Ondas and Palantir builds on the two companies existing collaboration and is the latest example in how the two companies are becoming increasingly intertwined.
Ondas and Palantir in March announced a strategic partnership to integrate Palantir's foundry product into Ondas' autonomous drone platforms worldwide.

"Regna AI extends our sovereign AI capabilities and creates opportunities to serve customers beyond our own hardware platforms," Brock said Thursday, adding that the new venture could expand the company's addressable market.
While there were many positives in Ondas' earnings, shares fell 8% to $5.27 on Thursday after ending Wednesday up 2.9%.
Shares of Ondas have been under pressure this year, falling 46% including Thursday's action, even as the company has seen solid revenue growth.
Palantir stock declined 0.2% to $172.05 on Thursday.

Among other defense plays, the iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense exchange-traded fund dropped 1.3%. Drone technology company AeroVironment and drone maker Karman Holdings fell 1.9% and 6.9%, respectively.
Drone maker Aevex surged 17% to $14.17 after posting 57% revenue growth in the third quarter.
